title: Phonon angular momentum transfer torque
authors: Verena Brehm, Daniel A. Bustamante Lopez, Shu Zhang, Dominik Juraschek
abstract: Angular momentum in solids is carried by (quasi)particles such as magnons, plasmons, and phonons, and coupling between these reservoirs enables diverse hybrid phenomena. Here, we introduce the transfer of angular momentum from lattice vibrations to magnetic order through the phonon angular momentum transfer torque (PAMTT), generated by a polarized phonon bath. We identify thermal routes for generating phonon angular momentum: a phonon Edelstein accumulation in noncentrosymmetric crystals and temperature-gradient-induced PAM currents with longitudinal Seebeck-like and transverse Hall components. Using realistic order-of-magnitude estimates, we find that PAMTT could produce measurable ferromagnetic-resonance frequency shifts and, for favorable interfacial coupling, drive magnetization reversal on nanosecond timescales.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to describe how angular momentum stored in lattice vibrations (phonons) can exert a torque on the magnetization of a magnetic material. By quantifying the Phonon Angular Momentum Transfer Torque (PAMTT), the authors predict measurable effects, including shifts in ferromagnetic resonance frequencies and the ability to drive magnetization reversal on fast timescales.
main_problem: The paper introduces and quantifies the transfer of angular momentum from lattice vibrations (phonons) to magnetic order via the Phonon Angular Momentum Transfer Torque (PAMTT). It explores thermal routes for generating this phonon angular momentum.
main_result: PAMTT can produce measurable ferromagnetic-resonance frequency shifts and possesses the potential to drive magnetization reversal on nanosecond timescales in magnetic materials.
method: The study uses theoretical formulation by adapting the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equation to incorporate the torque term derived from phonon angular momentum accumulation.
model_or_system: The system involves a magnetic layer whose dynamics are modeled by a macrospin description governed by the LLG equation. The coupling mechanism is the PAMTT, generated by phonon sources like the Phonon Edelstein effect or temperature gradients.
key_observables: Ferromagnetic-resonance (FMR) frequency shifts ($\Delta\omega$), magnetization switching time, and the magnitude of the torque ($	au_L$).
important_parameters: The strength of the PAMTT ($	au_L$), the anisotropy constant ($d_z$), and the coupling coefficients ($ eta_P,  eta_R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis simplifies the dynamics by assuming $\alpha=0$ and $ eta_R=0$ for the core LLG derivation, and it uses order-of-magnitude estimates for phonon accumulation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometries for PAMTT, including the Phonon Edelstein effect. Figure 2 (mentioned) shows the dependence of magnetization switching times on the strength of the PAMTT.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept of PAMTT and the thermal generation mechanisms (Edelstein, temperature gradient). It then develops the theoretical framework by modifying the LLG equation and presents order-of-magnitude estimates. Finally, it uses numerical simulations to predict measurable effects like FMR shifts and switching dynamics.
why_interesting: This work bridges lattice dynamics (phonons) with magnetism, providing a mechanism (PAMTT) to control magnetic switching and resonance frequencies using thermal gradients, which is relevant to understanding energy dissipation and control in spintronics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Geometries for PAMTT. A temperature gradient, indicated by the red-to-blue color gradient, generates a PAM accumulation or current according to (a, b) the phonon Edelstein effect [7, 8] and (c) the phonon angular momentum Hall effect [9, 10]. At the interface, the local PAM Lph = Llph exerts a torque on the magnetization m in the adjacent magnet. For the temperature-gradient directions shown here, the PAM is either perpendicular or parallel to the magnetization.
